 POTLAND (WGME) -- While a snowblower won’t be needed for any snow this week, those plowable storms will be here soon.
 It’s important to check your snowblower before you need to use it for the first time this season.
 Taking the necessary steps to ensure your snowblower is working properly now can prevent problems as winter approaches. (WGME) 
 You’ll first want to check the oil.
 “I would recommend that you check it and that it’s at the right level, change it if needed. Clean oil is best to have your machine run efficiently, start easier, that one of the main things to do,” Yerxa’s Power Equipment General Manager Nicole Yerxa said.
 Also read: When does snow usually arrive in Maine? A look at first-snow dates and records 
 If you want to be a little extra cautious, many shops, including Yerxa’s Power Equipment, will conduct a full tune-up.
 Taking the necessary steps to ensure your snowblower is working properly now can prevent problems as winter approaches. (WGME) 
 “They’re going to replace the sparkplug, they’re going to change your oil. They tip it up on end, and they take what we call the belly pan off, and they inspect your drive and your belts, grease your wheel shafts,” Yerxa said.
 If you have old fuel in your machine from last winter, there are a few things to keep in mind.
 Taking the necessary steps to ensure your snowblower is working properly now can prevent problems as winter approaches. (WGME) 
 “If it starts, your fuel is probably okay. If it’s starting hard or not starting, then you’re going to want to get that fuel out of there. We sell a product called mechanic in a bottle, you can put that in there and try to clean your fuel system, and if that doesn’t work, more than likely you need a carburetor cleaning,” Yerxa said.
 Also read: 'A true gift': Mystery $55,000 discovery in abandoned safe diverted to heating assistance 
 Once the new gas is in the machine, you can also purchase a stabilizer to help keep the fuel fresh throughout the season.
 Taking the necessary steps to ensure your snowblower is working properly now can prevent problems as winter approaches. (WGME) 
 “They do sell non-ethanol fuel, if you’re using that, then there’s no concern. If you’re buying it at the gas station, just don’t buy it way ahead of time. Just start your machine when they are calling for snow and make sure it seems to run,” Yerxa said.
 Taking these steps now can help you avoid problems as winter approaches.
